lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.title: Performance task build: deductibles premiums limits and exclusions

objective: Learners apply an invented deductible across multiple claims in a year and compute the policyholder's total cost.
scenario: Hyacinth is a made-up eighth grader modelling a pretend policy at $110.00 a month with a $750.00 deductible per claim, against two invented claims of $2,200.00 and $900.00 in the same simulated year.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: Compute a simulated year of Hyacinth's invented premiums.

prompts.text: What do 12 months of premiums cost?

tasks.directions: Apply Hyacinth's per-claim deductible to each invented claim and compute what the insurer pays on each.

prompts.text: How much does the insurer pay on the $2,200.00 claim?
How much does the insurer pay on the $900.00 claim?

tasks.directions: Total Hyacinth's own costs for the year and compare with bearing both claims unprotected.

prompts.text: What is Hyacinth's total cost for the year?
How much better off is that than paying both claims in full?

tasks.directions: The smaller claim barely paid out at all.

prompts.text: Explain why Hyacinth's $900.00 claim returned so little, and whether claiming at all on a loss near the deductible is worthwhile.

remediation: If a learner applies the deductible once for the year, mark the policy as per-claim and recompute each of Hyacinth's claims separately.
extension: Ask the learner at what claim size Hyacinth's payout would exactly equal the deductible, and what that means for claiming.
